entities.summary: Al-Kahina, also known as Dihya, was a Berber warrior-queen of the Aurès who played a pivotal role in the early 7th century Arab conquests. Born into a prominent Berber family, Al-Kahina ascended to the throne of her father, Al-Kahil, after his death in 700 CE. She skillfully navigated the complex web of tribal alliances and rivalries, leveraging her military prowess and religious leadership to unite various Berber tribes against their Arab neighbors. Al-Kahina's strategic victories and diplomatic maneuverings enabled her to maintain control over the Aurès region for nearly a decade, earning her the respect and admiration of her peers. Her legacy, however, was ultimately undone by the relentless pressure of the Arab conquests, which eventually led to her downfall in 703 CE. The loss of Al-Kahina marked a significant turning point in the history of the Berber people, as they were forced to adapt to a new era of Arab dominance. Despite her tragic end, Al-Kahina remains an important figure in North African history, symbolizing the resilience and determination of the Berber people in the face of overwhelming odds. The ancient Berber city of Makhala, where Al-Kahina was said to have been born, still stands today as a testament to her enduring legacy.
